title: Is It OK to Download Social Media Content? Ethics and Copyright
description: Is it OK to download social media content? Learn the difference between saving for yourself and reposting, why permission and credit matter, and more.
photoCaption: Download for yourself, not to reupload.
photo2Caption: Ask permission and credit the creator.
body:
Downloading videos or photos from social media is very easy these days. But an important question comes up: is it actually OK to download social media content, and what ethics and copyright principles should you keep in mind? This article covers it in general, simple terms, so you can save content with peace of mind without harming creators.

Note: this article contains general information, not legal advice. For specific legal questions, it's best to consult a lawyer or an intellectual property specialist.

Creators own their work

Every video, photo, piece of music or illustration uploaded to social media was made by someone. In general, the copyright in that work belongs to its creator, not to the people who watch or download it. Like many other countries, Indonesia also has laws that govern copyright.

In other words, just because anyone can see a piece of content doesn't mean it's free to use for anything. Publicly visible is not the same as copyright-free.

Download etiquette: watching it yourself vs reposting

There's a big difference between saving content to enjoy yourself and spreading it again.

Personal use

For example, saving a recipe video so you can watch it while cooking without internet, saving a tutorial to study, or saving a favorite video to rewatch. You're not claiming the work as your own and you're not sharing it with others.

Reposting

It's a different story if you upload someone else's content to your own account, especially without permission, without credit or to make money. This can infringe the creator's rights and the platform's rules. The consequences vary, from the post being removed and the account being restricted to legal trouble.

Etiquette before reposting someone else's content

If you want to reshare someone's work, follow these simple steps:

  1. Ask for permission. Message the creator and explain where and why you want to use the content.
  2. Wait for a clear answer. Silence doesn't mean yes. If you get no reply, it's better not to post it.
  3. Give credit. Mention the creator's name or account clearly, not tucked away somewhere hard to see.
  4. Don't remove the creator's identity. When reposting with permission, make sure the creator's name or account stays visible, for example in the caption.
  5. Respect the creator's decision. If the creator says no or asks for the content to be taken down, do as they ask.

If the platform has a built-in way to share, such as sharing a link or an in-app repost feature, that's often the safest option because the creator still gets the credit.

Always check each platform's rules

Every social media platform has its own terms of service that govern how content may be used and shared. The rules can differ from one platform to another and can change over time. Before using someone else's content for anything beyond watching it yourself, take the time to read that platform's terms.

Content that calls for extra care

  • Music and songs. The music in a video may belong to someone else, not the person who made the video.
  • Content showing other people. Respect the privacy of people who appear in videos or photos, especially children.
  • Commercial use. Using someone else's content for ads, sales or paid channels without permission is very risky.

Where does I Need Save fit in?

I Need Save is a tool for saving public posts from platforms like TikTok, Instagram, Facebook and X (Twitter) to your device. Private content, content that requires a login and region-restricted content can't be downloaded. Files are streamed directly from the original platform to your device and are not stored on the I Need Save server.

The tool is made to make personal use easier, such as watching offline. Responsibility for how content is used after it's downloaded stays with the user. So download for personal use, then ask permission and give credit before reposting.

If you're just getting started, our guides on how to download Instagram videos and Reels and where downloaded files are saved can help.

A simple principle that's easy to remember: saving something to watch yourself is different from spreading it. If you want to share it, ask permission and give credit.

Frequently asked questions

Is downloading videos to watch myself always allowed?

The rules can vary depending on the country, the platform and the type of content. Ethically, saving for yourself is very different from redistributing. For legal certainty, consult a professional.

If I give credit, can I repost without permission?

Not necessarily. Credit is a form of recognition, but it isn't the same as permission. It's best to still ask the creator first.

Can I use someone else's content to sell things?

Commercial use without permission is very risky. Contact the owner of the work to ask for permission or a license, and consult a lawyer if needed.
